NOTE:  PUBLIC PARTICIPATION INFORMATION
  Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each Open Session agenda item are
  available on the City's website under City Council Meeting agendas at rhe.city and during regular
  business hours in the office of the City Clerk. Meetings are live broadcast on the City's website and a
  recording is available for viewing after each meeting. Meetings are also broadcast on PVP-TV Channel 35
  (Cox) and Channel 39 (Verizon).

  Public Comment is welcome in-person on any item during City Council consideration of the item. Public
  correspondence may also be emailed to the City Clerk at laurenp@rollinghillsestates.gov. Emails
  received before 3:00 p.m. prior to the start of the meeting will be forwarded to the City Council for their
  consideration and included as part of the record. Members of the public may also comment online using
  eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos” page of the City’s website
  (www.rhe.city/MeetingAgendas). Once the agenda is published, there will be an “eComment” button next
  to the linked agenda under "Upcoming Events". Follow this link to the City’s SpeakUp page. After you
  register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda. These comments can be seen by the
  public, will be considered by the Council and become part of the record.

  An opportunity is also provided for the public to comment on non-agenda items concerning City matters. If
  you would like to address the City Council regarding an item on this agenda or make a general public
  comment, please complete a speaker sheet and give to the City Clerk.

MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  JUNE 13, 2023

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

MAYOR HUFF called the meeting to order at 7:02 p.m.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

Led by MAYOR HUFF.

3.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Stegura

City Council Members Absent:  Schmitz, Zerunyan

  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis

City Clerk read public comment received via email from resident Lisa Augustine, thanking the
City Council for its continued support of Pride Month.

B.  COMMEMORATING: DECLARING JUNE 19, 2023 AS JUNETEENTH

MAYOR HUFF declared June 19, 223 as Juneteenth.

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER inquired about the “construction without
planning/building approval” cases open in the annual Code Compliance Report, specifically
about educating the public about construction permitting requirements. Community
Development Director Naughton explained that staff strives to take an educational approach
when dealing with non-permitted construction, and that the website is a great resource for
education. COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER and MAYOR HUFF suggested information
be included in the City’s next community e-blast.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
JUNE 13, 2023
 6.  PUBLIC COMMENT/PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

Rolling Hills Mayor Pat Wilson thanked the City Council for its contribution of $18,000 in unused
Rule 20A funds to the City of Rolling Hills.

7.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

None.

8.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  RESOLUTION NO. 2546 AND COOPERATION AGREEMENT FOR THE CITY’S
  CONTINUED PARTICIPATION IN THE COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT BLOCK
  GRANT (CDBG) PROGRAM FOR THREE YEARS (FY 2024-27)

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve Resolution No. 2546 and the
  Cooperation Agreement authorizing the City to continue participating in the
  Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) Program through the Los Angeles
  County Development Authority (LACDA) for three years (Fiscal Years 2024-2027).

Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per the agenda material.)

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  SCHACHTER, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL
  VOTE:

  APPROVE RESOLUTION NO. 2546 AND THE COOPERATION AGREEMENT
  AUTHORIZING THE CITY TO CONTINUE PARTICIPATING IN THE
  COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT BLOCK GRANT (CDBG) PROGRAM
  THROUGH THE LOS ANGELES COUNTY DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY
  (LACDA) FOR THREE YEARS (FISCAL YEARS 2024-2027).

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Stegura
  ABSENT:  Schmitz, Zerunyan

City Clerk Pettit read Resolution No. 2546 by title.

B.  TRAFFIC & SAFETY COMMITTEE MEETING OF MAY 17, 2023: ACTION ITEMS
  RECOMMENDED FOR CITY COUNCIL APPROVAL

  Recommendation: That the City Council 1) Take no action on installing green
  pavement markings for the bike lanes on Palos Verdes Drive North; and 2) Direct
  staff to contract with Los Angeles County Department of Public Works to install and
  replace/relocate “No Parking” signs on the multi-use path located on the north side of
  Palos Verdes Drive North, as shown on the attached exhibit.

Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per the agenda material.)

Public Works Director Wahba explained where the signs are proposed on the pathway, in
addition to those on Palos Verdes Drive North, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  SCHACHTER, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL
  VOTE:
  1) TAKE NO ACTION ON INSTALLING GREEN PAVEMENT MARKINGS FOR
  THE BIKE LANES ON PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH; AND 2) DIRECT
  STAFF TO CONTRACT WITH LOS ANGELES COUNTY PUBLIC WORKS TO

JUNE 13, 2023
   INSTALL AND REPLACE/RELOCATE “NO PARKING” SIGNS ON THE MULTI-
  USE PATH LOCATED ON THE NORTH SIDE OF PALOS VERDES DRIVE
  NORTH.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Stegura
  ABSENT:  Schmitz, Zerunyan

C.  LETTER OF OPPOSITION TO SHERIFF CIVILIAN OVERSIGHT COMMISSION’S
  RECOMMENDATION TO INVOLUNTARY ROTATE DEPUTIES EVERY FIVE YEARS

  Recommendation: That the City Council authorize the Mayor to sign the attached
  letter to the Los Angeles County Board of Supervisor’s Office.

Management Analyst Slawson provided a staff report (as per the agenda material.)

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA noted that she agrees with the rationale behind this action of
the Commission, but the points raised in the letter are valid and important for the community.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  STEGURA, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  AUTHORIZE THE MAYOR TO SIGN THE ATTACHED LETTER TO THE LOS
  ANGELES COUNTY BOARD OF SUPERVISOR’S OFFICE.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Stegura
  ABSENT:  Schmitz, Zerunyan

9.  OLD BUSINESS

A.  AWARD OF PUBLIC WORKS CONTRACT TO WEST COAST FOOTINGS FOR
  RENOVATION OF ARENA #2 AT ERNIE HOWLETT PARK AND AGREEMENT WITH
  PORTUGUESE BEND NATIONAL HORSE SHOW EVENT ORGANIZERS FOR
  COST-SHARING OF THE PROJECT

  Recommendation: That the City Council 1) Direct staff to enter into a Public Works
  Contract with West Coast Footings (all to the satisfaction of the City Attorney), to
  renovate Arena #2 at Ernie Howlett Park in the amount of $89,272.13, with a
  contingency of $16,000 for a total project cost of $123,272; 2) Approve a Letter of
  Agreement between the City and PBNHS for 50% cost-sharing of the project.

Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas provided a staff report (as per the agenda material.)

City Attorney Davis explained that the Pepper Tree Foundation was added to the Letter of
Agreement since tax-deductible donations are being made to the Pepper Tree Foundation, in
response to COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA.

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER noted that the City needs to have the proper harrow to
maintain the footing throughout the year.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  STEGURA, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  1) DIRECT STAFF TO ENTER INTO A PUBLIC WORKS CONTRACT WITH
  WEST COAST FOOTINGS (ALL TO THE SATISFACTION OF THE CITY
  ATTORNEY), TO RENOVATE ARENA #2 AT ERNIE HOWLETT PARK IN THE
  AMOUNT OF $89,272.13, WITH A CONTINGENCY OF $16,000 FOR A TOTAL
  PROJECT COST OF $123,272; 2) APPROVE A LETTER OF AGREEMENT

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
JUNE 13, 2023
   BETWEEN THE CITY AND PBNHS FOR 50% COST-SHARING OF THE
  PROJECT.

10.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

None.

11.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA attended the South Bay Cities Council of Governments’
monthly Board meeting. She also attended the City Hall EV Charging Station ribbon cutting.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA reported that residents can get up to $150 for being part of
the Clean Power Alliance’s Power Response smart home charge program.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA noted that the Environmental Advisory Committee is
scheduled to meet on June 14, 2023.

MAYOR HUFF thanked COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA and staff for their efforts in the EV
Charging Station project at City Hall. COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA thanked the members
of the Environmental Advisory Committee for their participation in the project.

MAYOR HUFF attended the Green Hills Memorial Day event and the ribbon-cutting for See’s
Candy in the Peninsula Center with COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN. She thanked the Palos
Verdes Chamber of Commerce for their work on the successful annual Palos Verdes Street
Fair event. She also reminded the community about the upcoming Doors Open Peninsula 2023
event this Saturday, June 17. She also announced that Supervisor Janice Hahn will be hosting
a Town Hall with Sheriff Luna on Wednesday, July 12, 2023.

City Manager Grammer noted that he will be giving tours of City Hall on Saturday, June 17 as
part of the Doors Open Peninsula 2023 event.

12.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS

A.  REQUEST TO ATTEND CJPIA ANNUAL RISK MANAGEMENT FORUM

It was the consensus of the Council to allow any/all Council Members to attend the forum.

13.  CLOSED SESSION

None.

14.  ADJOURNMENT

At 7:45 p.m. MAYOR HUFF adjourned the City Council meeting to Tuesday, June 27, 2023,
at 7:00 p.m. for the purpose of a Regular Meeting.
